result.title: Beyond the Explicit: Benchmarking and Detecting Implicit Harm in Short Videos
result.summary: Short videos have become a dominant online medium, where harmful content is increasingly conveyed in implicit and fragmented forms. Prior work largely focuses on explicit categories, such as violence and hate speech, and often fails to detect videos that subtly promote misleading values through narrative context, emotional framing, or cross-modal cues, partly due to the lack of dedicated benchmarks for implicit harm. To bridge this gap, we construct DeepHarm-7K, a large-scale harmful short-video dataset comprising 7,110 samples annotated according to a fine-grained harmful-content taxonomy. The dataset systematically covers implicitly harmful videos across diverse real-world scenarios and is constructed through a rigorous multi-stage quality-control process. Building on this dataset, we propose DeepHarm-VL, a multimodal detection framework that integrates visual, audio, and cross-modal reasoning. The framework employs a two-round reasoning strategy to progressively identify surface-level evidence and infer latent harmful implications. Experimental results show consistent improvements over strong baselines and state-of-the-art methods across multiple open-source video-language models, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting both explicit and implicit harmful short videos.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 7,110 条短视频的隐式有害内容数据集 DeepHarm-7K，并提出融合视觉、音频与跨模态推理的 DeepHarm-VL 检测框架，用两轮推理先找表层证据再推断隐含危害。
AI.relevance_reason: 「latent」在此指隐含的有害语义而非模型内部推理状态，两轮推理为显式文本层面的分阶段提示，未涉及 latent 状态生成、使用或证据筛选机制，与 LVR 主线仅术语相近，缺少实质可借鉴线索。
